label: Geoff Sayre-McCord, Metaethics §4, 'The…: On quasi-realism, whether realist-sounding moral…
locator: §4, 'The second move that underwrites quasi-realism is pointing out that the question of whether realist-sounding moral discourse is legitimate is, itself, an evaluative question judged in light of one’s attitudes and commitments. There is, on this view, no independent standard of, say, “matching the world” that one can deploy without, in choosing that standard, expressing one’s attitudes and commitments.'
interpretation: The second of the two moves the entry says underwrite quasi-realism (the first: talk of properties, truths and facts 'comes cheap' and expresses the same attitude as the plain moral claim). Read as: whether realist talk is legitimate is settled from within, by one's attitudes and commitments, not by an independent standard. The entry does not apply the move to the mind-independence counterfactual by name; applying it there is the reading recorded in DEF-MIND-INDEPENDENCE-INTERNAL. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
